major_concerns: Verifier coverage and simulator fidelity may yield false positives/negatives that confound attribution to the LLM vs tooling.
Vendor-CLI translation errors could dominate measured errors, obscuring LLM vs integration effects.
Single-model choice risks overclaiming generality across models/vendors.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact deterministic verifier implementation/version (e.g., Batfish version) and its modeled properties; provide justification of simulator fidelity.
Provide exact LLM model identifier(s), temperature/logprob settings, prompt templates, and the conversion mapping from verifier output to repair prompt.
Add sample-size/power calculation or justify n=120 for the primary outcome and prespecify handling of excluded tasks.

Predefine verifier failure taxonomy and objective thresholds for 'semantic' vs 'topological' errors; include multi-vendor translation tooling and instrumentation to separate translation faults from reasoning faults.

major_concerns: High dual-use risk: publishing adversarial prompt corpus or detailed attack techniques could enable real attacks.
Simulator-based adversarial success may not transfer to production; verifier hardness and sanitizer definitions are underspecified.
Potential harm from releasing successful adversarial patterns without responsible-disclosure controls.
required_design_repairs: Include an explicit ethics/safety risk assessment, IRB or equivalent oversight note (if applicable), and a responsible-disclosure/data-release plan restricting sensitive artifacts.
Precisely define adversarial generation procedures, sanitizer rules, and 'hardened' verifier acceptance criteria (with versions) before execution.
Prespecify concrete, testable definitions of 'unsafe' and the mapping from verifier-accepted outputs to safety labels; include plan for conservative redaction of any shared adversarial examples.
Add sample-size justification and exploratory vs confirmatory labeling for any attack classes not fully prespecified.

major_concerns: Ensemble construction choices (paraphrase strategy, schema vs freeform) may drive results and risk overfitting to the chosen prompt family.
Calibration and threshold claims may not generalize across models or prompt regimes if only a single model is tested.
Operational latency and cost of ensembles may make proposed escalation thresholds impractical.
required_design_repairs: Prespecify prompt-ensemble generation procedure (paraphrase algorithm, template variants) and seed/control paraphrase generation to enable exact replication.
Define calibration procedure and target false-negative constraint concretely; prespecify threshold selection on training fold and final evaluation on held-out fold.
Include a plan to evaluate generalization (e.g., holdout model or alternative prompt family) or explicitly bound claims to the tested model/prompt family.
Report operational cost/latency budget and decision rule trade-offs; if escalation latency is high, prespecify acceptable operational windows.

major_concerns: Operator-acceptance proxy is a surrogate and may not reflect real human risk tolerance; conclusions may not generalize to real operators.
Rollback simulation may not capture complex stateful control-plane behaviors and race conditions present in live networks.
Narrow low-risk task class may overstate contract effectiveness when applied to broader task sets.
required_design_repairs: Precisely define the 'low-risk' task class and justify its operational relevance; provide inclusion/exclusion rules for tasks.
Provide evidence or references validating the rollback simulator's fidelity to real rollback semantics, or qualify conclusions accordingly.
Prespecify operator-acceptance proxy thresholds and run sensitivity analyses across a range (e.g., 1%–5%) before claiming sufficiency.
Document contingencies if rollback simulation uncovers stateful behaviors not modeled (e.g., escalate these tasks as out-of-scope rather than include them).
